sections.heading: A — Passing and parking
sections.markdown:
## A — Passing and parking
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers passing and parking for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC09-EXAM, WY-SEC09-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC09-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Passing and parking
sections.markdown:
## B — Passing and parking
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with passing and parking as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants study passing decisions, bicycle and heavy-vehicle clearance, blind spots and parking procedures.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

sections.heading: C — Passing and parking
sections.markdown:
## C — Passing and parking
FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Do not pass where a sign or pavement marking prohibits passing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Wait rather than passing when vehicles, pedestrians, bridges, curves, hills, intersections or railroad crossings are just ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
On a two-lane road, do not attempt to overtake more than one vehicle at a time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
Do not follow another vehicle that is itself passing a car ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not pass a school bus displaying flashing red lights unless a physical barrier or separate roadway lies between your vehicle and the bus. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Decide whether overtaking is necessary before beginning the passing maneuver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
Start the passing procedure at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Confirm that enough time and space exist to complete a pass safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
Signal and check around the entire vehicle before passing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
After those passing checks, increase speed and move into the passing lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Return to the right lane once the passed vehicle's front is visible in the rearview mirror. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook caps its qualifying passing-speed allowance at 10 mph above the speed limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
The qualifying passing-speed exception applies while overtaking a vehicle traveling below the legal maximum speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
Never pass on the right unless you can be sure it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn, provided the pass can be made safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
Leaving the pavement to pass on the right is unlawful. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
Safe passing on the right is also allowed when at least two lanes of heavy traffic are traveling in the same direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
Right-side passing is dangerous if another driver fails to see you and changes lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A03
Do not attempt to pass a bicyclist unless a clear, empty lane is available. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A03
Without adequate bicycle-passing space, slow to the cyclist's speed and follow until room becomes available. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0056]

sections.heading: C — Passing and parking
sections.markdown:
## C — Passing and parking
FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A03
Avoid remaining alongside a bicyclist for an extended time while sharing a single traffic lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A03
Reduce speed while passing a bicyclist to lower crash danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A03
When space permits, keep at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicyclist while passing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A04
When passing parked cars, watch for vehicles pulling into your path. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A04
Exhaust, illuminated brake or backup lights, a flashing turn signal, outward-turning front wheels or a seated driver can signal that a parked car may move. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A04
Watch for pedestrians or bicyclists emerging between parked cars to cross the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A04
Cutting in too soon after passing a truck and then slowing sharply leaves its driver little room or time to respond. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A04
Maintain a consistent speed while overtaking a large vehicle because the pass takes longer. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A04
Before returning ahead of a passed truck, make sure both headlights and the entire cab are visible in the rearview mirror. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A04
Account for a heavy vehicle's entire length, particularly double-trailer rigs, some of which can reach 100 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A04
Pass with enough speed to avoid lingering in the truck driver's blind spot. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A04
Lingering beside a truck can prevent its driver from taking evasive action without striking your unseen car. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A04
When approaching an emergency vehicle parked beside the road, move over or slow down. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A05
Heavy vehicles have a large blind spot directly behind them, so avoid tailgating in that No-Zone. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A05
Following closely behind a truck can hide your car from its driver and severely limit your own view of traffic ahead. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A05
Close following increases rear-end crash risk and exposure to debris such as ice, stones or tire material. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A05
A passenger car remaining in a large vehicle's side blind spot cannot be seen by that vehicle's driver. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A05
A truck's sudden lane change can cause a serious crash when a passenger vehicle occupies its blind spot. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A05
A right-turn squeeze occurs when a passenger vehicle is in a heavy vehicle's right-side blind spot as the heavy vehicle turns right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

Misconceptions: More lanes do not alone authorize passing on the right; heavy traffic must move in the same direction under the listed exception. A truck's high driving position does not eliminate its blind spots.
Mnemonics: Recall index: need, space, signal, mirror, return; this organizer adds no permission to pass where the source forbids it.
Glossary: Recall terms: no-passing zone, No-Zone, right-turn squeeze, physical barrier, parking brake and emergency flashers.
Dynamic facts: Passing allowances and parking restrictions remain edition-bound; posted prohibitions still apply. No phone or contact directory is used.

sections.heading: C2 — Passing and parking
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Passing and parking
FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
Parking beside the roadway side of another stopped or parked vehicle is unlawful. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
Do not park on a sidewalk, inside an intersection or in a crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A02
Parking is prohibited beside yellow-painted curb near an intersection or driveway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
Do not park alongside or opposite a street-construction site. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A02
Parking on a bridge or inside a highway tunnel is unlawful. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A02
Do not park where an official sign prohibits standing, stopping or parking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A02
Parking in front of a public or private driveway is unlawful. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A02
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A02
A vehicle parked in a designated disabled space must display a disabled placard or disabled license plates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A02
When parked uphill beside a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A02
For other hill-parking situations, turn the wheels toward the curb or road edge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A02
After parking on a hill, turn off the engine, take the keys and lock the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A02
Put all four wheels beyond the pavement for an emergency stop when possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A02
Do not make an emergency stop on a hill or curve where other traffic cannot easily see the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A02
Use the emergency flashers when making an emergency stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A03
Before leaving a parking space, look for approaching road users, especially bicycles and motorcycles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A03
Signal before starting to move out of a parking space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A03
When leaving a parking space, yield to approaching vehicles and motorcycles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A03
Enter traffic from a parking space carefully rather than darting into it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0060]
